title: Every keycloak-side interaction produces one structured audit event on an allow-list of fields
description: Each of the keycloak-side surfaces (discovery client, JWT verifier, introspection client, provider router, role adapter, sessionInventory) emits exactly one structured audit event per named interaction. Every event carries fields drawn from a fixed allow-list: `family` (one of `keycloak.discovery`, `keycloak.jwt`, `keycloak.introspection`, `keycloak.route`, `keycloak.roles`, `keycloak.session_inventory`, `keycloak.account_console`), `outcome`, `reasonClass?`, `realmSlug`, `sessionIdPrefix?`, `at`. No event may carry a token value (access token, id token, refresh token, introspection response body), a client secret, a raw claim record, or a substring of any of the above. The audit sink is contributed by the composed observability blueprint (or by a project-authored sink under the same interface); a sink failure logs a `keycloak.audit_sink_failed` warning event and never masks the underlying refusal.
rationale: The five TACs each require structured audit events with slightly different fields; without a cross-cutting REQ naming the allow-list and the token-exclusion rule, a reviewer cannot decide whether a new event field is inside the blueprint's contract. The REQ also anchors the sink-failure posture the guide implies but never states at REQ level.
